editorial:
Imagine going to a church lock-in for a fun night with friends, only for it to turn into a total nightmare. That is exactly what happens to a teenager named Justin. While the rest of the kids are just hanging out, Justin has a scary breakdown that leaves him shaken and silent for the rest of the trip. The vibe starts off feeling like a normal youth group event, but it quickly shifts into something much darker. You get to see the tension build as Justin tries to process the scary things he saw, while the adults in charge try to act like nothing happened. It feels like a mystery where you are trying to figure out if the horror is in Justin's head or if something truly evil is hiding in the church walls.

What really works here is the use of found footage, which makes the scary parts feel way more real. The acting feels natural, and the way the plot reveals the truth through the tape is a great touch. It does move a bit slow in the middle, but the payoff at the end is worth it. If you love movies that make you question who to trust, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends when the parents and church leaders finally watch the tape Justin recorded. The footage reveals that the lock-in was not a safe event at all. It shows that Justin was subjected to actual torture and evil acts by people he was supposed to trust. The twist is that the church leaders were hiding a dark secret. The film wraps up with the threat of criminal charges as the truth about the abuse comes to light.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found footage horror and psychological mysteries.
